assumptions: Tables follow the campaign_finance domain contract in domains/campaign_finance.yaml; donor_employer and donor_postcode are optional, and a source without either column yields no clusters.

limit_amount defaults to the 2025-2026 FEC limit for an individual giving to a federal candidate, $3,500 per election (https://www.fec.gov/help-candidates-and-committees/candidate-taking-receipts/contribution-limits/). Set it to the limit of the recipient type and jurisdiction under review; the UK has no donation limit (https://www.electoralcommission.org.uk/political-registration-and-regulation/financial-reporting/donations-and-loans).

The pattern matches what the FEC describes in conduit cases: someone at the limit gives money to others to contribute to the same candidate, or a corporation reimburses employees' contributions (https://www.fec.gov/updates/contributions-in-the-name-of-another-are-strictly-prohibited/).
Donors are matched by upper-cased name; postcodes are compared without spaces, so a 9-digit ZIP+4 matches only the same ZIP+4.
detectors.description: Donors who share an employer or postcode and each give one recipient an amount at or near the contribution limit within a few days.
false_positives: Colleagues often give together at a fundraiser their employer or a senior colleague hosts; that is lawful when each gives their own money.

Spouses and relatives at one address each have their own limit (https://www.fec.gov/help-candidates-and-committees/taking-receipts-ssf/limits-contributions-received-ssf/), so a household giving the maximum on one day is common.
Placeholder employers (for example INFORMATION REQUESTED or SELF-EMPLOYED) are excluded only when spelled as listed in the query; other spellings can form spurious clusters.
Large employers and dense postcodes produce clusters by chance; compare against the recipient's other donors before treating a cluster as a lead.
detectors.title: Maxed donor clusters

assumptions: Tables follow the campaign_finance domain contract in domains/campaign_finance.yaml; recipients.registered_date is the date the recipient registered with the regulator.
Only donations dated up to max_age_days after registration count, including any dated before it.

The pattern follows Campaign Legal Center complaints about pop-up committees: two super PACs formed within weeks of an LLC reported no contributions from any other source (https://campaignlegal.org/update/what-are-straw-donor-schemes-and-why-are-they-problem).
Donors are matched by upper-cased name.
detectors.description: A recipient that registered recently and received nearly all of its early money from one donor.
false_positives: Many legitimate committees start with seed money from their founder, a sponsoring organisation or an affiliated committee.
A single-candidate committee funded by the candidate's own money, or a party branch funded by its central party, has one funder by design.
The source may list only donations above a reporting threshold, so many small donors can be invisible and the top donor's share overstated.
A single funder is not proof of a straw donor; the lead is whether the funder had its own money, which needs company records and bank or filing evidence.
detectors.title: New recipient, single funder

assumptions: Tables follow the campaign_finance domain contract in domains/campaign_finance.yaml.

threshold defaults to the UK reporting threshold for donations to a party's central organisation, 11,180 GBP (https://www.electoralcommission.org.uk/political-registration-and-regulation/financial-reporting/donations-and-loans). For US federal candidates use the per-election limit, 3,500 USD in 2025-2026 (https://www.fec.gov/help-candidates-and-committees/candidate-taking-receipts/contribution-limits/).
A donor is one upper-cased name plus postcode when the source publishes one; the same person spelled two ways counts as two donors.
Amounts are compared as published; the detector does not convert currencies.
detectors.description: One donor gives one recipient several gifts, each below a threshold, that together reach the threshold within a short window.
false_positives: Regular monthly or recurring gifts reach any threshold eventually; a long window_days or low min_gifts flags ordinary supporters.

Published registers only list gifts above their own reporting thresholds or aggregated past them (UK parties report gifts over 2,230 GBP once a donor has passed the central threshold in a calendar year), so small split gifts may be missing or already disclosed as aggregations.

US committees can lawfully accept separate per-election contributions for a primary and a general election, and refunds or redesignations may follow; check the election designation and memo text of each gift.
Common names merge different people when the source publishes no postcode.
UK registers list a party's gifts per accounting unit (local branch) under one regulated entity, so one donor funding several branches on one day looks like split gifts to one recipient.
detectors.title: Structured gifts

The usual rate is total contacts over the months from the registrant's first to last contact with that institution, so quiet months count as zero.
detectors.description: Months in which one registrant's contacts with one institution jump far above its usual monthly rate.

assumptions: Generic. Runs on any lobbying register that fills the columns it reads (see the source's SKILL.md column mapping).

home_countries lists the register's home countries, spelled as the register spells client_country and separated by a vertical bar; left empty, the most common client_country in each register is the home country.

assumptions: Generic. Runs on any lobbying register that fills the columns it reads (see the source's SKILL.md column mapping).
Institutions match when the names are equal or one contains the other (six characters or more), case-insensitively; registers that spell institutions differently in the two tables miss matches.
A lobbyist is linked to a contact through the registrant, so the contact may have been made by a colleague.

detectors.description: A registrant's contacts with an institution where one of its lobbyists held public office, within a window after they left.

Broad institution names (a ministry) match many offices.

assumptions: Generic. Runs on any lobbying register that fills the columns it reads (see the source's SKILL.md column mapping).

detectors.description: Quarter-over-quarter shifts in spend (or, without money, registrant count) per issue area within one register's taxonomy.

assumptions: Generic. Runs on any lobbying register that fills the columns it reads (see the source's SKILL.md column mapping).

assumptions: Generic. Runs on any lobbying register that fills the columns it reads (see the source's SKILL.md column mapping).

assumptions: Tables follow the procurement domain contract in domains/procurement.yaml.
procurement_method uses the OCDS codes; limited and direct count as non-open, rows without a method are left out of the share and counted in unknown_method_processes.
The default min_share of 0.3 is the example threshold in OCP R013; iqr_upper_fence is the OCP alternative (Q3 + 1.5 IQR across the buyers shown).
detectors.description: Buyers that run a high share of their processes as limited or direct awards (OCP red flag R013).
false_positives: OCP R013: limited and direct methods have valid legal grounds such as urgency, sole sources, low values and framework call-offs.
Buyers that publish many framework call-offs as direct awards look non-open by construction.
detectors.title: High share of non-open procedures

assumptions: Tables follow the procurement domain contract in domains/procurement.yaml.
tender_published_date is the start of the submission period (OCDS tender/tenderPeriod/startDate, else the notice publication date) and tender_deadline its end.
Set min_days to the legal minimum for the buyer's jurisdiction and method; the default of 10 is a screen, not a legal threshold.
detectors.description: Open or selective processes whose submission period is shorter than a minimum number of days (OCP red flag R003).
false_positives: OCP R003: accelerated procedures for urgency, prior information notices and dynamic purchasing systems allow shorter periods legally.
A notice republished or corrected late shortens the apparent period.
detectors.title: Short submission period

assumptions: Tables follow the procurement domain contract in domains/procurement.yaml.
procurement_method uses the OCDS codes open, selective, limited and direct; rows without a method or a bid count are skipped.
number_of_tenderers counts bids for the process or lot the row describes (OCDS tender/numberOfTenderers or bids/statistics with measure bids).
detectors.description: Open or selective processes (or lots) that received exactly one bid (OCP red flag R018).
false_positives: OCP R018: niche markets, specialised goods or tight specifications can legitimately draw a single bidder.
Framework call-offs and lots reported with the parent notice's bid count can misstate competition per lot.
detectors.title: Single bid in a competitive procedure

assumptions: Tables follow the procurement domain contract in domains/procurement.yaml.
Supplier and buyer identifiers are stable within one source; names are not matched across sources.
Shares are by award value per buyer, award year, currency and category_code (R050 when filled, R040 when empty); an award with several suppliers is split equally between them.
The default min_share of 0.4 is the example threshold in OCP R040 and R050; min_awards keeps small markets out.
detectors.description: Suppliers that win a high share of one buyer's award value in a year, within one market when categories are known (OCP red flags R040 and R050).
false_positives: OCP R040/R050: small or specialised markets, incumbents on long programmes and buyers with few purchases concentrate legitimately.
Only the awards in the fetched sample count; a partial fetch inflates shares.
detectors.title: Supplier share outlier

assumptions: Tables follow the procurement domain contract in domains/procurement.yaml.
award_value is the value at award and final_value the current or final value after amendments, in the same currency; rows without final_value are skipped.
OCP R069 flags any increase; the default min_growth of 0.2 (20 percent) keeps small adjustments out.
detectors.description: Awards whose current or final contract value exceeds the value at award by a minimum ratio and amount (OCP red flag R069).
false_positives: OCP R069: amendments can be legitimate, such as exercised options, indexation and scope added through a documented change.
Where final_value is cumulative obligations (USAspending), incremental funding of an unchanged contract looks like growth.
detectors.title: Value growth after award
